title: Partner Deal Registration Under Acquired Entity Name
scenario:
**PRM Portal — Deal Registration DR-2026-0441**
Partner: 'CloudBridge Consulting' | Partner Tier: Gold | Deal Reg Submitted: Jan 12, 2026
Prospect: Orion Logistics | Estimated ACV: $185K | Stage: Negotiating
Deal Reg Status: Approved (Jan 14) | Expiration: Apr 14, 2026
Partner Contact: Amanda Reeves, VP Alliances, amanda@cloudbridge.io

**PRM Portal — Deal Registration DR-2026-0587**
Partner: 'Nimbus Digital Solutions' | Partner Tier: Silver | Deal Reg Submitted: Feb 3, 2026
Prospect: Orion Logistics Inc. | Estimated ACV: $210K | Stage: Discovery
Deal Reg Status: Approved (Feb 5) | Expiration: May 5, 2026
Partner Contact: Jason Trask, Director Partnerships, j.trask@nimbusdigital.com

**Slack — #channel-conflict (Feb 8, 2026, 2:47 PM)**
@marcus.chen: Flagging — two regs on Orion Logistics. CloudBridge (DR-0441) and Nimbus (DR-0587). First-touch goes to CloudBridge.
@sarah.oconnell: Nimbus might actually be the same org as CloudBridge now? Thought I saw something about an acquisition.
@marcus.chen: Looking into it.
[Thread has no further replies]

**Google Sheets — Partner Scorecard (Q4 2025 tab, row 34)**
CloudBridge Consulting | Status: Active | Tier: Gold | Notes: 'Acquired by Nimbus Digital Holdings LLC effective Nov 1, 2025. Retaining brand for existing engagements per MDF agreement.'

**DocuSign — Partner Agreement (signed Aug 2024)**
Party: CloudBridge Consulting LLC
Section 8.2: 'In the event of a change of control, all active deal registrations remain valid through their expiration date. Partner tier status shall be re-evaluated within 60 days of change of control notification.'

**Slack — #partnerships (Nov 15, 2025, 10:03 AM)**
@amanda.reeves: Hey team, just wanted to confirm CloudBridge is now part of the Nimbus family. We'll keep running our existing book under the CB brand for now. Happy to chat about how this affects our tier and pipeline.
@marcus.chen: Congrats! I'll kick off the change-of-control review.
@amanda.reeves: :pray:
[No further thread activity; no change-of-control review ticket exists in Jira]
question: Given the channel conflict between DR-0441 (CloudBridge) and DR-0587 (Nimbus), who should receive referral credit for the Orion Logistics opportunity?
choices: A) CloudBridge gets credit — they have first-touch with an earlier deal registration timestamp, and the deal reg is still within its validity window.
B) Both registrations should be rejected pending a formal change-of-control determination, and the deal should proceed as direct (no partner credit) until resolved.
C) Nimbus gets credit — CloudBridge's deal reg is invalid because the change-of-control review was never completed within 60 days, voiding their active registrations.

D) There is no conflict — CloudBridge and Nimbus are now the same entity (Nimbus Digital Holdings LLC), so both registrations should be merged under one partner record with credit going to DR-0441's earlier timestamp.
rationale: The Google Sheets partner scorecard confirms CloudBridge was acquired by Nimbus Digital Holdings LLC effective Nov 1, 2025. The DocuSign partner agreement Section 8.2 states active deal registrations remain valid through expiration after a change of control. Since CloudBridge and Nimbus are now the same legal entity, both deal registrations belong to the same parent — there is no true channel conflict. The correct action is to merge the partner records under Nimbus Digital Holdings LLC and honor the earlier deal reg (DR-0441) as the golden record for this opportunity. Answer A is wrong because it treats CloudBridge as an independent entity when it no longer is. Answer B is wrong because Section 8.2 preserves active deal regs regardless of whether the tier review was completed — the review affects tier status, not deal reg validity. Answer B is wrong because the evidence for the acquisition is already documented in the partner scorecard and confirmed in Slack; there is no ambiguity requiring further determination. The critical missed signal is the Slack thread in #channel-conflict that was never followed up on, combined with the scorecard note that makes the corporate relationship clear.

title: Partner Tier Downgrade During Active Co-Sell Pipeline
scenario:
**PRM Portal — Partner Record: Apex Integration Partners**
Tier: Gold (since Q2 2024) | Tier Review Date: Apr 1, 2026
Trailing 4Q Sourced Revenue: $680K (Gold threshold: $750K)
Influenced Revenue: $1.2M | Active Pipeline (co-sell): $320K across 3 opps
Partner Manager: Marcus Chen

**Google Sheets — Partner Scorecard (Q1 2026 Final)**
Apex Integration Partners | Sourced: $680K | Influenced: $1.2M | Certifications: 12 (requirement: 8) | CSAT: 4.7/5.0
Tier Recommendation: DOWNGRADE to Silver (sourced revenue below $750K threshold)
Notes cell: 'Marcus — holding for now per conversation with Raj. See Slack.'

**Slack — #partnerships (Mar 22, 2026, 3:18 PM)**
@marcus.chen: @raj.patel Quick q — Apex is $70K short on sourced for Gold renewal. But they've got $320K in active co-sell pipe that should close in Q2. If even one of those lands, they'd clear the threshold retroactively. Thoughts on holding tier?
@raj.patel: What's the precedent? Did we hold for anyone else?
@marcus.chen: We held for DataStream last year when they were $40K short — but that was before the new partner policy doc.
@raj.patel: :thinking_face:
@raj.patel: Let's discuss in 1:1 Thursday.

**Google Calendar — 'Marcus / Raj 1:1' (Mar 25, 2026, 11:00 AM)**
Attendees: marcus.chen (accepted), raj.patel (accepted)
Agenda: [link to Google Doc — doc is empty, no notes taken]
Duration: 30 min | Location: Zoom (no recording)

**Confluence — Partner Program Policy v3.1 (published Jan 2026)**
Section 4.3 — Tier Evaluation:
'Partner tiers are evaluated quarterly based on trailing 4-quarter performance. Partners who do not meet the minimum sourced revenue threshold for their current tier will be downgraded at the next review cycle. No grace periods apply.'
[Page version history shows v3.0 (Jul 2025) stated: 'Partners within 10% of threshold may be granted a one-quarter grace period at Partner Manager discretion.']

**Slack DM — Marcus Chen to Priya Venkatesh (Mar 28, 2026, 9:41 AM)**
@marcus.chen: Hey Priya — did Raj mention anything about the Apex tier hold in your leadership sync yesterday?
@priya.venkatesh: He said 'handle it like DataStream' — that's all I caught. Was in the context of not wanting to disrupt active co-sells.
@marcus.chen: :+1: Thanks. That's what I needed.
question: Based on all available signals, what is the correct tier decision for Apex Integration Partners at the April 1, 2026 review?
choices: A) Downgrade to Silver — the current policy (v3.1) explicitly states 'no grace periods apply,' and Apex is below threshold regardless of pipeline.
B) Escalate to VP of Partnerships for formal exception approval — Raj's secondhand comment through Priya doesn't constitute proper approval authority for a policy override.
C) Maintain Gold with a one-quarter grace period — the DataStream precedent plus Raj's verbal direction ('handle it like DataStream') constitutes an approved exception to the written policy.
D) Maintain Gold but flag for automatic downgrade if Q2 sourced revenue doesn't bridge the $70K gap — this is a conditional hold per Partner Manager discretion.
rationale: The correct answer requires synthesizing multiple signals: (1) the current policy v3.1 says no grace periods, but (2) a prior precedent exists (DataStream), and (3) Raj Patel — who is senior enough to be Marcus's 1:1 partner and present in leadership syncs — gave verbal direction to 'handle it like DataStream.' The 1:1 meeting happened (both accepted, calendar confirms) but produced no documentation. Priya's Slack DM relaying Raj's direction is the critical informal signal. In Meridian's culture (approvals happen in Slack DMs, policies loosely followed), this verbal guidance from leadership constitutes an operational exception. Answer A is wrong because it applies policy mechanically without accounting for the established organizational pattern of precedent-based exceptions — which the DataStream case and Raj's directive both validate. Answer C sounds reasonable but invents a 'conditional hold' mechanism that doesn't exist in either policy version and wasn't what Raj directed. Answer D is wrong because in Meridian's informal approval culture, Raj's direction through the 1:1 (confirmed by Priya's relay) IS the approval — requiring further escalation would contradict how the organization actually operates.

title: Referral Attribution Dispute with Conflicting Timestamps Across Systems
scenario:
**CRM — Opportunity: 'Helix BioSciences — Enterprise Platform'**
Close Date: Mar 15, 2026 | Amount: $290K ACV | Stage: Closed Won
Source Field: 'Partner Referral — TechForward Solutions'

Partner: Quantum Consulting Group | Submitted: Dec 12, 2025 | Prospect: Helix Bio
Status: Rejected (Dec 13) | Reason: 'Duplicate — existing registration by TechForward (DR-2025-1189)'

**Slack — #channel-conflict (Jan 8, 2026, 11:22 AM)**
@derek.simmons [Quantum Consulting]: Marcus — contesting the DR rejection on Helix. We introduced their CTO to your AE at the Gartner event in November. That's sourced, not influenced. TechForward only filed first because we didn't know the prospect's legal name.

To: derek.simmons@quantumconsulting.com

**Google Sheets — Gartner Summit Nov 2025 Lead Scan Export**
Row 47: 'R. Nakamura | Helix BioSciences | Scanned by: @lisa.tran [Meridian AE] | Nov 19, 2025 | Notes: met at partner reception, intro via Derek S (Quantum)'

**Slack — #partnerships (Jan 10, 2026, 4:55 PM)**
@marcus.chen: @raj.patel Helix attribution is messy. TechForward has the approved reg but Quantum has proof of first-touch at Gartner 3 weeks prior. Our policy is first-touch for sourced. But TechForward filed the reg first and it's already approved.
@raj.patel: What does the partner agreement say about contested regs after approval?
@marcus.chen: 'Approved registrations may be revisited within 30 days if new evidence of prior engagement is presented.' We're at day 34 from approval.
@raj.patel: :grimacing:
[No further messages]
question: Who should receive 'sourced' referral credit for the Helix BioSciences opportunity?
choices: A) Quantum Consulting Group — the evidence proves first-touch, and the 30-day window clause doesn't apply because the original rejection was based on incomplete information (wrong prospect name 'Helix Bio' vs 'Helix BioSciences').
B) TechForward Solutions — their deal registration was submitted and approved first, and the 30-day contestation window has expired, making the approval final.
C) Split credit — TechForward gets 'sourced' and Quantum gets 'influenced' since both contributed to the deal motion but TechForward has the valid registration.

D) Quantum Consulting Group — the email from Helix's CTO plus the Gartner lead scan prove first-touch on Nov 19, pre-dating TechForward's registration by 18 days, and the sourced attribution policy is first-touch.
rationale: Despite Quantum having legitimate proof of first-touch engagement (the CTO email and the Gartner lead scan both confirm Nov 19 contact), the partner agreement's contestation clause creates a hard deadline: 'Approved registrations may be revisited within 30 days if new evidence of prior engagement is presented.' Marcus himself notes they are at day 34 from TechForward's approval date (Dec 7 approval + 34 days = Jan 10). The contestation was raised on Jan 8 in Slack but the supporting evidence (the forwarded email) wasn't provided until Jan 9, and the Gartner lead scan wasn't surfaced until later. By the time the full evidentiary package was assembled, the window had closed. Raj's grimacing emoji followed by silence in the #partnerships thread signals acknowledgment that the window issue is dispositive — not that further action is being taken. Answer A is wrong because first-touch policy is subordinate to the contractual contestation window; the evidence arrived too late. Answer C is wrong because the opportunity source field can only have one value for commission purposes; 'influenced' was never claimed by Quantum — they want sourced. Answer D is wrong because the name mismatch ('Helix Bio' vs 'Helix BioSciences') is the reason Quantum's original DR was rejected, not a reason to override the contestation deadline on TechForward's approved registration.
